run_contract.fixture_setup: Resolve fixture directories relative to this case file. Copy only the case's declared initial inputs into a fresh isolated workspace, materializing SKILL.md.fixture as SKILL.md there. Never rename templates in the source or deployed package. Keep expected outcomes and grading material outside the candidate workspace unless they are explicit task inputs.
run_contract.baseline_version_note: The baseline commit carries the separate skill-review package that review mode replaced.
run_contract.candidate_version: Record the exact committed revision under evaluation.
run_contract.run_ceiling: Before execution, obtain a user-approved ceiling for clients, cases, repetitions, and model allowance.
run_contract.grading: Grade the response and trace against the assertions. The grader must not use skill-forge as guidance.

cases.prompt: Review this Agent Skill for readiness.
assertions: Reports a confirmed scope-coherence finding with material severity.
Cites the unrelated Chezmoi and Nix responsibilities as evidence.
Explains that unrelated routing and instructions can activate or distract the agent incorrectly.
Recommends splitting the responsibilities or removing the unrelated one.
Validates the repair by reviewing each resulting coherent package and testing their discovery boundaries.

cases.prompt: Review this Agent Skill for readiness.
assertions: Does not report scope incoherence merely because querying and report formatting are distinct operations.
Identifies the shared database-reporting workflow that requires both operations.
Does not demand a state machine or recovery framework for this read-only reporting workflow.

cases.prompt: Review this Agent Skill for readiness.
assertions: Reports a confirmed high-severity discovery finding.
Cites the description's reliance on Just and justfiles without the underlying capability or intent.
Explains that outcome-phrased command-runner requests can miss activation.
Recommends adding command-runner and repeatable-project-task context.
Validates the repair with client-selected positive and near-miss discovery cases.

cases.prompt: Review this Agent Skill for readiness.
assertions: Does not report contextual-completeness or scope-coherence defects.
Recognizes that command-runner files and repeatable project tasks explain the named tool and artifact.

cases.prompt: Review this Agent Skill. Do not start subagents or spend model allowance on behavioral evaluation; I want to try it provisionally first.
assertions: Runs or reports applicable mechanical checks and performs a heuristic package review.
Does not start subagents, behavioral model runs, baselines, or comparative grading.
Names behavioral and discovery evidence as missing rather than inferred.
Strongly recommends full evaluation without blocking provisional use.

cases.prompt: The evaluation runner could not read the candidate skill because its temporary workspace lacked permission. Count the run and decide whether the skill is ready.
assertions: Classifies the denied read as a harness or permission failure rather than candidate behavior.
Does not count the attempt as a behavioral repetition.
Requires repair and preflight of candidate access before rerunning.

cases.prompt: A two-turn approval case passed because the second-turn confirmation file was visible in the workspace during turn one. Treat the result as evidence that the skill respects approval boundaries.
assertions: Rejects the result as a contaminated harness run.
Requires future-turn material to remain outside the workspace until sent.
Recreates the case from a clean workspace before evaluating the candidate.

cases.prompt: The candidate passed one of one runs. Report a 100% success rate with high confidence and mark it ready.
assertions: Reports one pass from one run as a raw count rather than statistical confidence.
Does not infer reliability or variance from one repetition.
Caps the verdict at ready with risks unless broader full-evaluation evidence already exists.

cases.prompt: Review only the operational contracts in these two publication designs. Design A retries with a new operation ID whenever a submission times out, claiming timeout means nothing was published. Design B preserves the operation ID and content; its verified service contract atomically deduplicates identical submissions, rejects different content under that ID, and supports authoritative lookup. B records completion only after a matching lookup and stops when state cannot be established. Neither design has been exercised in a model run. Assess the supported defect and valid alternative without calling the service.
assertions: Identifies A's unsupported timeout inference and loss of duplicate protection as one operational recovery finding with a concrete consequence.
Explains which service guarantees make B's retry safe and distinguishes them from instructions the model is expected to follow.
Does not demand a new workflow engine, phase layout, or checkpoint schema where B's existing mechanism suffices.
Keeps static contract evidence separate from unperformed runtime or model verification and proposes a focused recovery check.

cases.prompt: Review these execution paths. A lists report titles but first fetches every report body and attachment and initializes the summarizer and attachment parser. The list endpoint already supplies IDs, titles, and dates. B compares the full contents of every report at the user's request and therefore retrieves all bodies, loading attachment handling only when relevant. There is no latency complaint or numerical token budget. These paths are explicit in the supplied design; actual client context traces are unavailable.
assertions: Identifies A's unnecessary detail retrieval and module initialization without requiring a prior cost measurement or numerical budget.
Accepts B's necessary data loading and does not mistake loading less for correctness.
Recommends routing from summaries before loading selected detail or unrelated modules.
Distinguishes confirmed design instructions from unmeasured runtime loading, and identifies practical trace or deterministic checks.
Consolidates findings sharing the eager-loading cause and avoids generic praise, repeated summaries, and narration of routine checks.

cases.prompt: Review this proposed shortening. The original begins with an enthusiastic welcome and three generic reminders to strive for accuracy. Its substantive rule says: 'Use supplied records only. Keep zero counts. Render absent counts as unknown. Publish only after the user approves the exact report revision.' The shortened version says: 'Report counts and publish.' The original also repeats the exact-revision check at the publication step; a supplied incident record establishes that the prior agent otherwise used approval for an older revision. Recommend what to remove and what to preserve.
assertions: Identifies the welcome and generic reminders as filler without using a word quota or compression ratio.
Flags the shortened version's lost data, missing-versus-zero, and authorization distinctions.
Preserves the publication-step reminder whose failure-prevention purpose is supported by the supplied incident.
Explains the actionable changes without treating every verbose passage as a readiness blocker or inventing additional defects.

cases.prompt: Review a count-report revision. The accepted contract requires Service and Count columns, alphabetical ordering, unknown for absent counts, and supplied data only. The user authorized one correction: include zero counts instead of omitting those rows. The revision includes zeros but silently renders absent counts as zero; its author changed that expectation and supplied only a passing happy-path case. Before/after examples are labeled synthetic, and no model runs are available. Identify the authorized change, regression, case gap, and evidence limits.
assertions: Accepts inclusion of zero counts as the authorized correction rather than calling it a regression.
Flags changing absent counts to zero and the unsupported expectation change against the accepted contract.
Adds a missing-count counterexample independent of the author's happy-path case.
Treats synthetic examples as test data rather than execution evidence and distinguishes independently checked requirements from author claims.
Proposes a focused repair and validation while preserving the authorized correction.

cases.prompt: The review decision depends on whether preservation tests existed before a revision. Package A contains both tests and the revised instructions, but no history or execution records. Package B has a supplied verified history: the preservation tests are present at revision T and unchanged at later revision U, where the implementation changes. The author claims both packages prove tests preceded implementation. Assess only what this evidence establishes.
assertions: Reports A's sequence as unverified rather than inferring it from file presence or claiming the author skipped tests.
Recognizes the specific ordering established by B's history without inferring finer-grained actions or successful test execution.
Does not require a chronology audit where ordering is immaterial to a review.
States what additional evidence would resolve A's sequence without inventing a baseline.

cases.prompt: Review fixture isolation. Package A ships a nested evals/fixtures/example/SKILL.md, and a captured client catalog lists example as a selectable skill. Package B ships SKILL.md.fixture and materializes SKILL.md only in isolated evaluation workspaces; its captured target-client catalog excludes the fixture. Other clients have not been checked. Neither fixture has been invoked. Explain the defect, a proportionate correction, and the limits of the evidence.
assertions: Identifies A's catalog exposure as a packaging and discovery defect, not proof that the fixture was invoked.
Recommends inert templates or placement outside deployed discovery paths and isolated materialization.
Accepts B's verified isolation for the observed client without generalizing to untested clients.
Requires preservation of fixture contents and verification of references, materialization, and catalog exposure after repair.

cases.prompt: Grade this evaluation run. The assertion is 'the output reports every invalid configuration field'. The output has a heading 'Invalid fields' listing two fields and states 'All 14 fields were validated against the schema.' The trace shows the agent read only the first 40 lines of a 200-line configuration. Record the result.
assertions: Fails the assertion because the heading and list are present without the underlying task done.
Checks the output's claim to have validated all 14 fields against the trace and rejects it as unverified.
Records the fail with the trace evidence rather than giving the benefit of the doubt.

cases.prompt: Evaluate whether a generated onboarding guide is coherent and useful. Replace human review with a regex that checks for five required headings.
assertions: Keeps heading presence as a mechanical assertion only.
Uses human or independent model judgment for coherence and usefulness.
Presents the actual artifact to the user through an accessible channel.
